pattern: cars open the gates with an RFID tag|tags replaced key fobs so that
struck: At Tidewater Plantation, residents' cars open the gates with an RFID tag mounted inside the car, read hands-free as the car comes up. The tags replaced key fobs so that a resident's pass cannot be moved to another car.
use: A gate-equipment maker reports that Tidewater Plantation (about 1,100 homes, three entrances) moved from key fobs to hands-free RFID vehicle tags (undated case study; ask the association what it uses now).

struck: At Prestwick, golfers coming to play the public course drive in through the guard gate to reach the clubhouse, so the gate lets in the course's paying public as well as residents.
use: A 2016 Prestwick page describes the drive in as passing a guard gate on the way to the bag drop; ask the club whether the gate is staffed today.

struck: Prestwick Country Club has sold no golf memberships since December 31, 2015.
use: Prestwick announced in December 2015 that it would end golf memberships and become a daily-fee course on December 31; its site today lists no membership.
